proposal.name: Fit big numbers in the dashboard's tiles

plan.name: Fit big numbers in the dashboard's tiles
plan.summary: The states tile's 1,285,100 is wider than its tile, so the dashboard's six number tiles get their words from the server, where tests can reach them: Tiles(t Totals, who Who) []Tile, in a new internal/dashboard/tiles.go, builds them in the page's order, keyed bad, states, stmts, bugs, proved and dec, each with its Label, Shown (what the tile reads), Small (its small text) and Title (its tooltip) in the words the page uses now, and the snapshot carries them as tiles, for everything and for each repository from its own totals, so choosing a repository shows its own. A number of a million or more shows short, to three significant figures with no trailing zeros and M, B or T, as 1.29M, 1.5M, 123M or 1B, and its tile's small text and tooltip both lead with it exactly, as "1,285,100 states, across 15 models, exhaustively, within the ratified bounds"; below a million a number shows in full, with its small text as now and no tooltip, and the page counts it up as now. Each tile also gives its number's width in em, Ems, counting a figure at 0.7, a comma or point at 0.4, a slash at 0.6 and any other sign at 1, more than any of them takes in the page's font, and the page sets the number no larger than its tile's inside width over that, with the numbers row's tiles as size containers (not the projects table's cells, which share the num class) and a counting number sized for the wider of where it counts from and to. So a number that would be wider than its tile is set smaller until it fits, at six, three or two tiles to a row and every width between. SPEC.md and the README don't describe the tiles, so neither changes.

tests.name: TestABigNumberShowsShortWithItsExactNumberNearby
tests.says: 1,285,100 states show as 1.29M, with "1,285,100 states, across 15 models, exhaustively, within the ratified bounds" as the tile's small text and its tooltip, and 999,999 shows in full, with its small text as now. A million or more rounds to three significant figures, as 1M, 1.5M, 12.3M, 123M, 1B and 1.23B, and every one of the six tiles shows 3,456,789 as 3.46M, with the exact number in its small text and tooltip, and 999,999 in full.

tests.name: TestEveryTilesNumberFitsItsTileAtEveryWidth
tests.says: For totals from none to 999,999,999,999 of everything, every tile's number comes with a width in em at least what its signs can take in the page's font: a figure 0.7 em, a comma or point 0.4, a slash 0.6 and any other sign 1. Set as the page sets it, no larger than its tile's inside width over that, it fits inside its tile at every width from 320 to 1,440 px, with six, three or two tiles to a row as style.css lays them out, and with totals like today's, 1.29M among them, no number is set smaller than 30 px.

tests.name: TestEachRepositoryShowsItsOwnTiles
tests.says: The snapshot carries the tiles of its totals, and each repository the tiles of its own totals, so a repository without the decision log shows 0 decisions where Invariant's own shows the 2 in its log.

tests.name: TestThePageReadsEveryTileField
tests.says: The page's script reads every field of a tile, and the tiles of the snapshot and of each repository.

usage.summary: The plan passed its check on the first try: the server now builds the six number tiles, so 1,285,100 shows as 1.29M with the exact number in the tile's small text and tooltip, and each number comes with a cautious width estimate the page uses to shrink it until it fits. The fit test can't render the page, since the factory's sandbox runs only Go, so it checks that estimate against the page's layout from 320 to 1,440 px using per-character widths I chose to be generous, not ones measured from the page's actual font.
